referenceDevice: BPI-R4 (MediaTek MT7988A/Filogic 880), combined EthWAN + EasyMesh Controller/Agent build (production-style image)
measurementCondition: 60-second aggregate and per-process /proc/stat and /proc/<pid>/stat time-delta sample; all 4 cores online at governor default; light real-world background activity (OneWifi, snmpd, and napi/phy0 Wi-Fi softirq threads all show measurable, nonzero activity, indicating some radio activity during the window) but no controlled client/traffic load applied. Not a controlled loaded-workload test.
notes: First real per-process CPU breakdown captured for this profile (prior captures had only the aggregate figure). Per-process percentages are normalized to % of total system capacity across all 4 cores, matching the aggregate figure's own normalization — NOT % of a single core. (An earlier version of this capture's tooling computed per-process percentages against one core only, which does not sum consistently against a multi-core aggregate; that has been corrected here.) othersCpuPercent (2.0%) covers kernel worker threads (kworker/*, ~0.16% of that) plus many near-idle kernel/IRQ threads each individually below measurable resolution at this sample rate. OneWifi is the largest single consumer at 0.55% (of total system capacity); onewifi_em_ctrl and onewifi_em_agent — despite their large and growing memory footprint (see memory-footprint companion file) — show minimal CPU activity here (0.01% each), consistent with idle/light-load conditions rather than active mesh operation. This remains an idle/light-load result; a loaded sample (EasyMesh formed, active Wi-Fi clients, sustained WAN throughput) has not yet been collected, and the profile's assumed hardware NAT/flow offload capability (see Section 3, CA-007) has not been confirmed or refuted by this measurement either way.
